appearance.organs.leaf.shape.width.why: A blade's shape word says how broad it is for its length; between two words, between their breadths.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.leaflet_wid.why: A compound leaf's shape word is its leaflets': it says how broad each is for its length, as a simple blade's does.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.outline.why: A blade's shape word says where it is widest and how its sides run; between two words, the outline between theirs. Cordate, reniform and deltate blades have bases a width along the blade cannot draw, and wait for a card that can.

generator.defaults.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.defaults.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.width.note: Each word's width over length lies inside the band the Systematics Association's chart of plane shapes gives it, the value in the band the model's choice: lanceolate and oblanceolate 3:1 to 6:1 (0.25); elliptic, ovate and obovate 3:2 to 2:1 (0.57, 0.6, 0.6); orbicular about 1:1 (0.95); linear longer than 6:1, its sides parallel (0.08). The chart gives oblong and spatulate by their sides, not a band: 0.4 and 0.35 are the model's. A flora's two words ("ovate to lanceolate") read as the forms between them, so the width is their middle.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.leafl.note: A compound leaf's shape word describes its leaflets, so a leaflet's width follows the same chart as a blade's. Each word's width over length lies inside the band the Systematics Association's chart of plane shapes gives it, the value in the band the model's choice: lanceolate and oblanceolate 3:1 to 6:1 (0.25); elliptic, ovate and obovate 3:2 to 2:1 (0.57, 0.6, 0.6); orbicular about 1:1 (0.95); linear longer than 6:1, its sides parallel (0.08). The chart gives oblong and spatulate by their sides, not a band: 0.4 and 0.35 are the model's. A flora's two words ("ovate to lanceolate") read as the forms between them, so the width is their middle.

rules.appearance.organs.leaf.shape.outli.note: Outlines drawn to the Systematics Association chart's definitions: lanceolate and ovate widest below the middle, oblanceolate and obovate above it, elliptic and orbicular at it, linear and oblong with their sides parallel, spatulate a broad rounded tip on a long narrow base. The curves are the model's, each the half-width as a share of the widest at 15 places from the base (u 0) to the tip (1), the same places for every word, so two words that tie draw the outline halfway between theirs. An ellipse for elliptic and orbicular, a rounded rectangle (a superellipse of power 4) for oblong. A compound leaf's word is its leaflets' (spec rework P4).
